items.title: Eddie Marshall interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 8, 2002
items.q: We were playing all these Woody Herman things

ctx.x: Yeah. Well I played a little bit. I played in an Army band but I was — by the time — I got drafted into the Army. I was living in New York as a young man and having problems with drugs, and hit sort of like a rock bottom. And when I got drafted, there were like all soldiers and I wanted to get out of, whatever. You couldn’t get out of Basic.

I didn’t know anything about anything that was going on in the world when I got drafted. This was like ’62. I was just so totally involved with myself and music, that I didn’t know there was a war going on in Vietnam or it was something I didn’t really pay much attention to, politics and all that stuff. And so I got in the Army, I did get in a band, I was at Fort Dix, New Jersey, but something was happening. It was something in the air like in ’63, we started getting all of these Asian officers coming to Fort…
